risk_if_not_implemented: Without Contingency Plan Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned, critical business processes and services may not withstand or recover from disruption, causing extended outages and data loss. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Lack of oversight of internal controls (R-GV-6), Incident Persistence / Recurrence (R-IR-3), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption (MT-25).

compensating_control_1.name: Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to incorporate lessons learned from analyzing and resolving cybersecurity and data protection incidents to reduce the likelihood or impact of future incidents.
compensating_control_1.justification: Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned (IRO-14) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Contingency Plan Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned (BCD-11) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Contingency Plan Testing & Exercises
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct tests and/or exercises to evaluate the contingency plan's effectiveness and the organization's readiness to execute the plan.
compensating_control_2.justification: Contingency Plan Testing & Exercises (BCD-10) provides periodic assessment and assurance that compensates for the absence of Contingency Plan Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned (BCD-11) by providing structured evaluation of the environment to surface gaps and verify residual control effectiveness. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
